goal: Build the floor. The big picture, number systems and signed numbers carry the vocabulary every later lesson assumes, and they take longest to sink in, which is why they go first while there is still room.
drill: The exam questions are inside each lesson. Answer every one in the Big Picture, Number Systems and Signed Numbers before you stop. Then stop by ten; tomorrow is long.

window: Thursday evening, 6:30 pm to 11:00 pm, after the Java paper
goal: Start with fifteen minutes, book shut, recalling Monday's number work. Then every calculation topic in one run: floating point, image sizing, instruction formats, addressing and performance. All formula work with a worked example to copy under pressure.
drill: The exam questions inside those lessons. Anything you miss, reread that block before moving on.

goal: Pipelining and cache, which carry more marks on this paper than anything else and sit inside the compulsory Question One. Then RISC against CISC for the objective half.
drill: Every pipeline and cache question inside those two lessons. They are Question One's heaviest parts.

window: Friday, 11:00 am to 1:30 pm, before the paper at 3
goal: Sit Question One of both papers against the clock, then the floating point, instruction format and pipeline questions you will choose for your other two. Finish on the one page night before sheet, then eat and stop.
drill: In the hall: Question One is compulsory. For the other two, choose floating point, instruction formats with image sizing, and pipeline timing.
